## Summary
`scripts/verify-contracts-in-linux.sh` (v1.16.1) installs vendor CLIs at fixed defaults: Claude Code `2.1.265`, Codex `0.154.0`, OpenCode `1.18.29`. A macOS developer runs it exactly to prove the real-client areas for *their* setup. But by default it proves an older Claude Code and Codex than the ones they actually use (here Claude Code 2.1.289 and Codex 0.158.0). It still reports green, and `result.json` does not flag the mismatch. The version drift that broke real users before (#609, #617, #628) is exactly what this run then misses.

## Expected
- By default, prove the versions installed on the host: read `claude --version`, `codex --version` and `opencode --version` before starting the container, and install those versions inside it. Fall back to the CI pins only for a client that is not installed, and say so.
- Add `--client-versions ci|installed|latest` to choose explicitly.
- `client_preparation` in `result.json` records `source: installed|ci-pin|latest`. The summary line warns when the proven version differs from the host's installed version.
- Optionally, also prove the newest published version of each client, so a release that breaks Router is caught before users update.

## Acceptance
- On a host with Claude Code 2.1.289, the default run proves 2.1.289, and the summary says so.
title: verify-contracts-in-linux.sh proves CI-pinned client versions, not the versions installed on the host
